classification.difficultyReason: Express the height using a closed box's surface-area constraint, then substitute into its volume formula.

content.prompt:
A closed box with a rectangular base has length three times its width.

The width is $x$ cm and the total surface area is $216\text{ cm}^2$.

Show that the volume is $V=81x-\frac{9x^3}{4}$.

spec.description: Unlabelled tall closed rectangular box with visible front, top and right faces. Depth recedes upwards to the right. All visible edges are solid black; no hidden edges or face shading.
spec.mathematics: A rectangular prism illustrating the closed box. The drawing supplies no additional measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: No answers or derived dimensions are shown.

sizing.reason: Restore the source-calibrated full figure height and width; preserve all drawing coordinates, camera, extrusion and native label font size.

answer.worked:
Let the height be $h$ cm. The length is $3x$ cm and the width is $x$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}
2(3x)(x)+2(x)(h)+2(3x)(h)&=216\\
6x^2+2xh+6xh&=216\\
6x^2+8xh&=216\\
h&=\frac{216-6x^2}{8x}\\
h&=\frac{27}{x}-\frac{3x}{4}
\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}
V&=3x\cdot x\cdot h\\
V&=3x^2\left(\frac{27}{x}-\frac{3x}{4}\right)\\
V&=81x-\frac{9x^3}{4}.
\end{align*}$$
The volume is measured in $\text{cm}^3$.
